tfn.s: Nordelta was built on land where capybaras already lived.
tfn.why: The text says: "Nordelta was built on wetland, where capybaras already lived."

tfn.s: No living rodent is bigger than the capybara.
tfn.why: The text says capybaras are "the world's largest living rodents".

tfn.s: The resident who fired the gun was arrested.
tfn.why: The text mentions complaints and an investigation, but does not say whether anyone was arrested.

tfn.s: All residents of Nordelta enjoy having the animals nearby.
tfn.why: The text says: "Other people are much less happy."
The text says they "usually live in groups near rivers, lakes and wetlands".

focus.note: A collocation is a pair of words that go together naturally. Learn them as a pair, like take a photograph.

tfn.s: The capybaras were living in the area before Nordelta was developed.
tfn.why: The text says they "survived while a human settlement expanded around them".

tfn.s: Everyone in Nordelta reacted to the capybaras in the same way.
tfn.why: The text says some people are delighted, while others report damage and risks.

tfn.s: Nordelta residents have voted on whether to move the capybaras.
Moving the animals would be difficult even if residents agreed to it.
tfn.why: The text says moving a group "only works if there is somewhere suitable to move them to".

tfn.s: The shooting incident was the first time residents argued about the capybaras.
tfn.why: The incident "revived a long-running argument", so the argument already existed.

focus.note: Verbs and nouns often come in fixed pairs. Choose the verb that native speakers actually use with the noun, not one that only seems logical.

items.s: Residents are being forced to ____ sides in a public dispute.

tfn.s: The writer implies that the capybaras' behaviour on the lawns is typical of the species.
tfn.why: The text calls it "entirely ordinary wetland behaviour, performed in an extraordinary setting".

tfn.s: The writer treats relocation as an easy solution.
tfn.why: Relocation "depends on there being somewhere suitable to move the animals to", which the development has done away with.

tfn.s: The investigation into the shooting has concluded.
tfn.why: The text says an investigation followed but not how it ended.

tfn.s: The writer considers the word "invasion" misleading in this case.
tfn.why: The text says what some call an invasion is "better understood as the survival of wildlife".

tfn.s: Nordelta's artificial lakes make the area less attractive to capybaras.
tfn.why: The text says the waterways "have proved attractive habitat" for them.

speak.title: Role-play: a capybara on the lawn
speak.setup: Work in pairs. Read your card, then have the conversation. Swap roles and do it again.

a.text: Capybaras keep eating your garden and you're worried about your dog. Explain the problem and ask what the community will do. You can accept a plan, or ask for something different.

b.text: You think the animals were here first. Listen to the resident, then suggest ways to share the space. Try to find a plan you both accept.

phrases: They were here long before the houses.
What do you suggest we do?
I'd be happy to try that.
That isn't fair to the animals.
speak.after: Afterwards, tell the class: what plan did you agree, and who gave up more?
